title: Illusion in the Ruins Shocks the Truth
next_chapter_hook: Eerie laughter echoes from the depths of the ruins. Chen Ji must make a choice before his Heavenly Fate runs out—whether to force his way into the unknown depths or retreat and seek another path?

text.content: Ye Qing's words, pregnant with meaning, pierced Chen Ji's heart like a fine needle. The Tianji Record is a shackle—how could he not know this? Yet there was no time to dwell on it. The entrance to the ancient ruins slowly opened, and a desolate, primeval aura rushed toward him, carrying the dust of decay and spiritual energy fluctuations that had not dissipated for countless millennia. Chen Ji stood at the stone steps before the ruins' entrance, staring at the deep, bottomless corridor. His expression was calm as usual, but at the depths of his pupils there was a faint flicker—that was the vigilance honed through countless moments on the edge of life and death. 'Shackle or weapon, it matters not,' he murmured to himself, his voice so faint it was barely audible, 'My life, Chen Ji's life, has always been in my own hands.' With that, he stepped into the ruins, his steps steady, his figure disappearing into the darkness.

The interior of the ruins was far more grand than imagined. Giant stone pillars lined both sides of the corridor, their surfaces covered with mottled ancient runes that, despite millennia of wear, still faintly emanated a ghostly blue glow. The air was filled with an indescribable smell—like aged blood mixed with withered spiritual herbs, causing one to feel faintly nauseated. Chen Ji walked slowly forward, all his spiritual senses fully activated, yet he felt an invisible force quietly suppressing his perception. With each step, the stone bricks beneath his feet emitted a low rumble, as if the entire ruins were scrutinizing this uninvited guest. His right hand slightly raised, fingertips gently stroking the location of the fragment on his chest—where a faint warmth was emanating. That was the Tianji Record issuing a warning. Danger lies ahead.

At the end of the corridor stood a massive underground stone hall. The hall's vaulted ceiling soared into the clouds, its apex inlaid with countless dim spiritual stones, resembling the remnants of stars scattered across the night sky. At the center of the stone hall stood a black altar, above which floated a mass of churning gray mist. Within that mist, lights flickered vaguely, as if something terrifying was sealed within. The moment Chen Ji stepped within the stone hall's range, the fragment on his chest violently trembled—that vibration was intense to the point of scorching, unlike any previous foresight. The characters on the fragment began to appear on their own, golden light piercing, illuminating Chen Ji's face. His heart lurched; instinctively he wanted to suppress it, only to discover this time it was not the Tianji Record showing him something—it was the fragment itself being forcibly awakened by some force within these ruins. He frowned, gazing at the gray mist, feeling an unprecedented unease rise from his tailbone straight to his fontanelle.

Golden light blazed. Chen Ji's consciousness was violently yanked into a chaos, the world spinning as everything before his eyes abruptly transformed. When he opened his eyes again, the scene before him left him frozen in place. The stone hall was gone, the gray mist was gone, replaced by a gloomy underground prison. The prison was woven from dozens of thick rune chains, each chain inscribed with dense prohibition patterns. At the center of the intertwined chains, a figure floated mid-air. It was a woman. Her clothes were tattered, her appearance withered and haggard, her former beauty worn down to pallor and emaciation. Yet that face—even eroded by time and suffering—Chen Ji recognized at a glance. It was his missing sister. Chen Nian.

Chen Ji's breath completely froze at this moment. He stared fixedly at the imprisoned figure, his pupils contracting violently, his hands unconsciously clenching into fists. His fingernails deeply embedded in his palms, the sharp pain could not distract him in the slightest. Chen Nian—he had searched for his sister for several entire years, countless nights of restless tossing, countless midnight dreams showing that innocent, cheerful face. But the Chen Nian appearing before him now had her eyes tightly closed, her lips pale and dry, so withered she resembled a dried corpse. Her four limbs were pierced through by rune chains, the chains deeply embedded in her bones, crimson blood dripping down the chains and pooling into a shocking pool of blood beneath her feet. The air was thick with a heavy smell of blood, so acrid it nauseated. Chen Ji's chest felt as if gripped by an invisible hand, a suffocating fury erupting from the depths of his heart, scalding until all the blood in his body boiled.

The scene in the illusion continued to evolve. Chen Ji's gaze swept across his surroundings, discovering that Chen Nian was not the only one imprisoned in this prison—there were several robed figures standing outside the cage. Their faces hidden beneath hoods, emanating a strong demonic path aura. One of them was projecting a stream of spiritual energy toward the center of the cage, that energy upon touching Chen Nian's body transformed into a blinding golden light, spreading along the rune chains and illuminating Chen Nian's entire body. At that moment, Chen Ji saw the full picture of the runes on Chen Nian. Those were not ordinary prohibitions, but a formation forcibly inscribed into her flesh, tendons and bones through extremely cruel methods. Every rune was deeply fused with the blood within her body, meaning—she had been imprisoned for far too long, long enough that these prohibitions had become part of her body.

dialogue.content: 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key...' A hoarse, ancient voice rang in Chen Ji's mind—it was Mo Xiansheng's voice, 'What is sealed within her is the core of ancient prohibitions capable of shaking the very foundations of heaven's way. The Holy Sect spent a hundred years of painstaking effort, laying this scheme, merely to await a specific bloodline capable of opening it.' Mo Xiansheng's voice paused, his tone uncharacteristically carrying a trace of heaviness, 'And that bloodline is precisely the Chen family line.'

text.content: Chen Ji's body trembled slightly. The Chen family line—these four words struck like a heavy hammer, shattering his last remnant of blind hope. He had long suspected his and his sister's origins, suspected why the Tianji Record would choose this so-called waste. But he never imagined the truth would be this cruel. The Holy Sect had begun laying plans over a century ago, and he and Chen Nian, from birth, were destined to become pieces in this chess game. His sister was imprisoned and tortured to become the key opening a certain forbidden door; while he himself was chosen by the Tianji Record—to become another manipulated piece. He took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the surging emotions, his gaze refocusing on Chen Nian in the illusion. This time, he observed more carefully. The rune formation patterns on Chen Nian's body bore a striking resemblance to some of the patterns on the Tianji Record fragment. This was definitely no coincidence.

Just then, the Chen Nian in the illusion suddenly showed signs of movement. Her eyelashes quivered slightly, then slowly opened her eyes. Those were eyes that had lost all spark, hollow and despairing, as if her soul had long been extracted from her body. Yet the moment her gaze swept across the void—she seemed to sense something. Within those dead eyes, suddenly a faint yet fierce light ignited. She saw Chen Ji. Even separated by the barrier between illusion and reality, even tortured beyond human form, Chen Nian still recognized her brother. Her lips began to quiver and move, seemingly wanting to say something, but no sound could emerge. Chen Ji stared intently at the shape of her lips, deciphering her meaning word by word. 'Brother... I'm... waiting... for... you...' Five words, faint as a candle guttering in the wind, yet serving as the last thread of sanity preventing Chen Ji from completely losing control.

Chen Ji's eye sockets instantly reddened. Rage was like a beast trapped in a cage, crashing wildly within his chest, crashing until his internal organs throbbed in agony. He wanted to roar, wanted to charge into the illusion and shatter those rune chains, wanted to dismember the Holy Sect's beasts a thousand times. Yet his reason firmly suppressed this impulse. This was an illusion, not reality; what appeared here was merely a phantom, not the real Chen Nian. He recited silently in his heart, his fists clenched until his knuckles turned white, the intense pain from his fingertips反而让 his thoughts grew clearer. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out again: 'Boy, anger saves no one. If you want to save her, you need sufficient strength and intelligence. Right now you need to make a decision—'

The illusion continued to expand. Chen Ji saw those robed figures begin to converse, their words reaching his ears in fragments. '...The lock key is fully mature, the final ritual can be conducted in three more months...' '...Then using the Chen family's blood as the guide, the Heavenly Fate seal can be completely opened...' '...If that boy dares to come, we can round them all up in one sweep, saving us the trouble of searching everywhere...' Chen Ji's pupils abruptly contracted. Three months. Only three months of time. In three months, the Holy Sect would use Chen Nian to complete the final ritual. And the so-called 'Chen family blood'—the 'that boy' they mentioned, clearly referred to himself. He felt a bone-piercing chill rise from the soles of his feet straight to his fontanelle. This was not merely a trap; it was a deadly game already woven for him. From the start, the Holy Sect knew of his existence, and perhaps even secretly guided the direction of the Tianji Record's inheritance—leading him step by step to this place, merely waiting for him to walk into the net himself.

Chen Ji's expression flickered uncertainly in the golden light of the illusion. His brain operated at high speed, disassembling, reorganizing, and deducing every piece of information he had just obtained. Three months—this was the time window he currently possessed. Too short, too short for him to leisurely lay out plans; yet it cannot be said to be completely useless, at least better than being completely in the dark. He now faced three paths: first, while the illusion had not yet dissipated, forcibly track the source of this illusion, directly lock onto the location where Chen Nian was imprisoned, and rescue her at the fastest speed possible; second, suppress his impulses, first gather more intelligence, thoroughly understand the Holy Sect's arrangements and guard forces at this location, and act when the time is ripe; third, temporarily withdraw from this place, seek alternative solutions to rescue Chen Nian from other channels—such as Ye Qing's demonic path connections, or the still un unsealed information within the Tianji Record fragment. Each path had its advantages and disadvantages, and time was the resource he lacked most.

However, just as Chen Ji was weighing the pros and cons, the scene within the illusion suddenly changed. Those robed figures seemed to sense something, all lifting their heads to gaze toward the direction outside the prison. One of them's voice abruptly rose: 'What rat dares spy on the Holy Sect's forbidden grounds!' Chen Ji's heart shuddered—they had detected his observation. Immediately afterward, a cold, bone-piercing spiritual pressure gushed forth from the depths of the illusion, like materialized killing intent, directly striking Chen Ji's consciousness. The illusion began to violently distort, the image of Chen Nian imprisoned like a shattered mirror bursting into fragments. In the last moment before his consciousness was forcibly yanked back to reality, Chen Ji saw Chen Nian's lips move again. This time, she said: 'Don't... be... reckless...' Then, everything fell into darkness.

choice.prompt:
The illusion shattered, and Chen Ji returned to the stone hall. His mind still echoed with Chen Nian's 'Don't be reckless' warning, and the approaching footsteps and cold laughter of those robed Holy Sect members. He must make a decision within an extremely short time—the unknown dangers in the depths of the ruins, the three-month time shackle, and his sister's eyes full of hope—each factor tore at his reason.

Chen Ji, what will you do?

choices.description: Track the illusion's source recklessly, lock onto Chen Nian's position at the fastest speed before guards are fully alert, even if it means exposing one's location.
choices.visible_cost: Consumes Large Amount of Heavenly Fate
choices.visible_reward: May Directly Locate Chen Nian's Imprisonment Site
choices.risk_hint: Extreme Risk—Solo Deep Entry into Enemy Territory, Life Threatening

text.content: Chen Ji tightly clenched his fists, a decisive and fierce glint flashing in his eyes. He took a deep breath, no longer suppressing the spiritual energy within his body, allowing the Tianji Record fragment to vibrate madly. Golden light burst from his chest, illuminating the entire stone hall as bright as day. Following the lingering spiritual energy traces of the illusion, he fiercely darted toward the depths of the ruins. His footsteps echoed through the spacious stone hall, interweaving with his rapid breathing. He knew he was taking a risk, walking directly into the Holy Sect's trap—but so what? Chen Nian was waiting for him. Waiting for far too long. Even if the path ahead was a dragon's pool and tiger's den, he would charge through it.

However, just as Chen Ji was about to dash into the deep corridor, a sinister laugh rang out from the darkness. 'Heh, as expected, you came. The Chen family's whelp，果然沉不住气.' Several shadows flashed out from both sides of the corridor, completely blocking his path. Chen Ji's footsteps abruptly stopped, yet his expression showed no panic whatsoever. He slowly raised his head, his gaze coldly sweeping across those shadows, his voicecalm得可怕: 'Get out of the way.' Merely two words, yet carrying a killing intent that made one's spine chill.

choices.description: Calm down and prioritize gathering intelligence, obtain as much information as possible about the Holy Sect's guard deployment and Chen Nian's situation without exposing one's location.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial intelligence, reduce risk of subsequent operations
choices.risk_hint: Low risk—but may miss the optimal rescue timing

text.content: Chen Ji forcibly suppressed the surging killing intent and anxiety in his heart, the near-mad fierce glint in his eyes gradually replaced by calm. He stepped back, hiding his figure within the shadow of a stone pillar, while his fingers rapidly formed incantations, using the power of the Tianji Record Fragment to trace a concealment rune in the void. A flash of golden light, and his presence instantly merged with the darkness of the stone hall. He did not immediately retreat, but observed the approaching black shadows from the shadows, carving their clothing features, spiritual fluctuations, and positioning layout into his mind one by one. Holy Sect guards—three Foundation Establishment cultivators—this might not have posed much threat to him on an ordinary day, but at this moment he was alone deep within enemy territory; any head-on confrontation would be a losing strategy.

After recording everything he saw and heard, Chen Ji quietly retreated backward. His movements were light and silent, like a ghost lurking in the night. Only after completely leaving the stone hall's range did he slightly quicken his pace, while rapidly calculating in his heart. Three Foundation Establishment guards—with his current cultivation, there was no chance of victory in a direct confrontation, but this also meant the Holy Sect's level of attention to this place was limited; they hadn't expected any outsiders to intrude. This was both good and bad. Good because the enemy was arrogant; bad because it might mean they possessed absolute confidence, confident enough not to need more personnel arranged. He clenched his fist, already forming a plan in his heart.

choices.description: Temporarily exit the ruins, utilize the Demonic Path's network or the Tianji Record Fragment to unseal information, seeking a covert rescue route that won't alert the Holy Sect.
choices.visible_reward: May discover more covert rescue routes
choices.risk_hint: Medium risk—requires external assistance, risk of information leakage

text.content: After quickly weighing the options in his heart, Chen Ji made the most prudent yet agonizing decision—retreat. He knew that with his current strength, charging into the Holy Sect's Forbidden Grounds would be no different from courting death. And Chen Nian's final lip-reading of 'Don't act rashly' was like an alarm bell, constantly reminding him not to be reckless. He quietly exited the stone hall along the path he came, his figure disappearing into the darkness of the corridor. The golden light of the Tianji Record Fragment had already faded, but he could still feel that burning sensation—the Fragment was transmitting some kind of message to him, as if there was more content yet to be unsealed. Regarding the connection between the Chen family's bloodline and the Heavenly Fate Lock Key, regarding the true purpose of the Holy Sect's century-long scheme... The answers might lie within those unopened pages of the Tianji Record.

The moment he exited the ruins, Chen Ji let out a long breath of turbid air. The night breeze brushed his face, carrying the unique fragrance of grass and trees from outside the ruins, forming a stark contrast to the lingering scent of blood in his mind. He looked up at the night sky—stars desolate, moonlight cold and clear, just like his current state of mind. Three months—he only had three months. He needed to find a foolproof plan before the Holy Sect completed their final ritual. This would inevitably become a race against time. He slowly clenched his fist, his knuckles cracking. Holy Sect... he remembered this debt. When the time was ripe, he would personally settle this account, with interest. In the distance, the runes at the ruins entrance slowly dimmed, as if no one had ever intruded upon this place.

choices.memory_label: 陈机对夜清的信任度提升——他决定向魔道圣女寻求帮助

text.content: Regardless of what choice Chen Ji made, the lingering resonance after the illusion shattered would not fade for a long time. Standing in the night wind outside the ruins, his mind constantly replayed Chen Nian's eyes filled with hope and pleading, along with her tragic appearance—her limbs pierced by formation chains, blood flowing profusely. Each recollection felt like a dull knife slowly cutting through his heart, the pain almost unbearable. Yet Chen Ji was no ordinary person. He was the one who survived as atrash in the Tianqing Sect for years, the one who navigated carefully amidst the struggles of three major sects. He was the one who never abandoned thinking and scheming even after being chosen by the Tianji Record. Rage could burn, but it could not consume everything. He took a deep breath, pressing that killing intent that threatened to shatter his reason deep into his heart, wrapping it with cold calculation, turning it into motivation for progress.

Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze sharp as a blade. He stared at the gradually dimming runes at the ruins entrance and said coldly: 'Holy Sect... Chen Ji swears enmity with you that cannot be resolved!' The moment his words fell, the night wind howled past, as if witnessing his oath. His voice echoed across the empty mountain wilderness, startling a flock of night-roosting birds. In the distant mountain forest, something seemed to be watching him from the shadows, but Chen Ji did not look back. He knew that from this moment on, everything was different. He was no longer the worthless servant-disciple who moved cautiously for self-preservation; he now had a clear goal—to rescue Chen Nian, to destroy the Holy Sect's conspiracy, and to make those who dared to harm his sister pay a hundredfold, a thousandfold price. The night was deep as ink, with scattered stars. Chen Ji's silhouette stretched long under the moonlight, like a sharp sword about to be drawn from its sheath.

Chen Ji stood still in the night wind for a while, only departing after the burning sensation in his chest completely subsided. He walked down the mountain path, his mind already rapidly sorting through all the information gathered that night. Heavenly Fate Lock Key, three-month deadline, Chen family bloodline, final ritual—each piece of information was dismantled, reorganized, and deduced, constructing an incomplete but direction-guiding sketch. Chen Nian's imprisoned location had been initially locked within some forbidden grounds of the Holy Sect, but the specific coordinates still required further investigation. The Holy Sect's guard strength was weaker than he had anticipated—this meant they either possessed absolute confidence or were currently deploying their main forces to other more urgent matters. Either situation was a variable he could exploit. A cold, faint smile curved at the corner of his mouth, though there was no笑意 in his eyes. Three months—would be enough.

After leaving the ruins area, Chen Ji found a concealed mountain cave and sat cross-legged to regulate his breathing and concentrate his mind. He did not rush to leave; instead, he closed his eyes and repeatedly replayed everything he witnessed that night in his mind. Every detail—the black-robed cultivators' clothing, the arrangement of the runes, the connection between the formation binding Chen Nian and the Tianji Record Fragment—all were dismantled one by one, searching for clues that might have been overlooked. After a long while, he opened his eyes, a complex expression flickering within them. Some of the runes on the Tianji Record Fragment were actually from the same source as the formation imprisoning Chen Nian. What did this mean? Was the Tianji Record itself part of the Holy Sect's plan, or had the Chen family's fate been entangled with some even more ancient power from the beginning? Either answer pointed to the same truth—this game of chess was far grander and deeper than he had imagined. He lowered his head to look at the faintly glowing Fragment on his chest and murmured: 'What exactly are you?' The Fragment offered no words, only that warm sensation responding to his question.

The night deepened, the mountain wind grew colder. Chen Ji sat still in the cave for a full hour, and only after sorting out his chaotic thoughts did he rise to leave. He did not immediately return to the Tianqing Sect, but instead found an inconspicuous inn in a nearby market town. He needed time, needed intelligence, needed a thorough plan. Three months—long in some ways, short in others. If he followed the conventional path of cultivation to increase his strength, time would be far from sufficient; but if he took an unconventional path, leveraged others' strengths against them, victory was not entirely impossible. In his mind, he outlined a preliminary chess game—Ye Qing's Demonic Path network, Su Qingyao's influence within the sect, even those old foxes who harbored hostility toward him could become usable pieces under specific conditions. A faint smile curved on Chen Ji's lips—that smile was calm yet dangerous, like a venomous snake lurking in the shadows. 'Holy Sect, oh Holy Sect,' he murmured, 'you think Chen Ji is meat being delivered to your door? Then走着瞧吧.'

The next morning, Chen Ji woke early. Morning light streamed through the window lattice into the room, casting mottled patterns on the floor. He stood before the window, gazing at the bustling stream of people in the market town, his expression calm as usual, as if last night's earth-shattering discovery had never occurred. Yet only he himself knew that the seed called 'revenge' had already taken deep root in his heart, sprouting, taking root, and flourishing at an alarming rate. He turned to retrieve pen and paper from the table, writing down the key information witnessed last night: the approximate location of the Holy Sect's forbidden grounds, the spiritual characteristics of the three Foundation Establishment guards, the formation structure binding Chen Nian, and the imminent 'three-month' deadline. With each word written, the coldness in his eyes deepened a degree. After finishing, he tucked the note into his chest, keeping it close to his body. Then he pushed open the door and strode into the morning light. The new game of chess had already begun placing its pieces. And this time, he would move first.
